payload.text: max_ease is applied by the COMPILER, not only by the runtime, and a config whose ease is greater than or equal to its dwell is refused by name. THE DEFECT IS SPLIT ENFORCEMENT, NOT AN UNLUCKY PAIR OF CONSTANTS -- cc's correction, verified from source f593de8: showreel:799-800 applies min_dwell and min_ease and NEVER applies max_ease, while the cap lives only in player.html's easeOf, at the Math.min(..., LIM.max_ease) token -- cited by token because 3903937 moved it off the line 549 this row named until 2026-09-09, whereas the two showreel citations here were swept the same day and are correct, and showreel:988 comments 'the runtime enforces the same floors' when it enforces one the compiler does not have. One limit, two homes, disagreeing, and a comment asserting a parity that does not hold -- this thread's own dominant class, in the code about to be ported. README section 7's claim that compiler and player both enforce the floors is false for max_ease.
